title: Zero first column forces zero determinant
statement: Let $p,m$ be natural numbers and let $R$ be a list of natural-number rows. If, for every $i<m+1$, the first entry of row $i$ (taken as zero when absent) is zero modulo $p$, then the determinant modulo $p$ of the matrix of size $m+1$ formed from $R$, with missing entries taken as zero, is zero.
hypotheses_covered: For every $i<m+1$, the first entry of row $i$, taken as zero when absent, is zero modulo $p$.
